s1_sub: Bukowy Dwór — Thermal Spa & Health Resort × ElevenLabs
s1_tagline: Native conversational agent deployment for a demanding 60+ guest base across a spa resort chain.
s1_badge: Phase V1 & V2: Case Study, Product Design & System Architecture | 2026
s1_notes: Start with 30 seconds of business context: why a health resort and why seniors, before touching the technology.
s2_title: Senior Guests Wait. Front Desk Can't Keep Up.
s2_cards: The 60+ demographic strongly prefers voice calls over mobile apps and web forms.
Call surges at 8:00–10:00 and 16:00–18:00 create busy lines and guest frustration.
An unanswered call is a lost treatment ($30–$80) or room booking ($100–$250).
Staff are overloaded with check-ins and have no bandwidth for pre-arrival outbound calls.
s2_notes: This is the business problem slide. Before explaining your solution, ask the interviewer what questions the problem raises for them.
s3_title: Who Is Calling? Mrs. Sophia, 72 Years Old.
s3_points: Speaks slowly, pauses naturally mid-sentence, takes time to think before answering.
Does not recall clinical treatment names — asks for “that massage that helps my lower back”.
If the bot interrupts or fails to understand twice, a senior hangs up immediately.
Expects a clear SMS summary, often asked to be sent to her daughter.
Every technical parameter (3.0s timeout, 0.85x pace, paraphrasing) stems directly from this persona.
s3_notes: Stress that this is not an abstract persona — it is the archetype of a health-resort patient.
s4_panel_body:
• Integrated loop: STT + LLM + TTS in a single WebRTC/SIP channel

• Response time: ~430 ms instead of >2.0 s in a classic cascaded backend

• Strict grounding: answers come only from the 5 RAG files

• Tool calling: native webhooks into the hotel PMS

• Deterministic handoff: transfer to reception whenever in doubt
s4_notes: Why a native ElevenLabs loop? Latency elimination. A cascade of three services loses a senior guest inside two seconds of silence.
s5_decisions: A cascaded pipeline (STT -> external LLM -> TTS) adds more than 2 s of latency. The native ElevenLabs loop drops to ~430 ms. For a senior, every second of silence erodes trust.
Flash is ultra-fast but sounds technical. Eleven v3 Conversational (280 ms) delivers warmth, intonation and empathy. For a 70+ guest, a natural voice matters more than 100 ms.
The default 1.2 s timeout cuts in while a senior takes a breath. turn_timeout: 3.0 s, turn_eagerness: Patient and speed: 0.85x remove the stress.
s5_notes: Show that you know the cost and the trade-offs: when to pick Flash, and why v3 wins in a health resort.
s6_left_body:
• 01_access.md — parking, shuttle, step-free access
• 02_spa_catalogue.md — 7 treatments and pools
• 03_rooms_and_pricing.md — 3 room types
• 04_restaurant.md — diabetic and light diets
• 05_procedures.md — house rules and safety

RAG mode split:
• Prompt Mode (in context): pricing + procedures
• Auto Mode (semantic search): descriptions and access
s6_right_body:
• Strict grounding:
No information in the knowledge base = immediate transfer to reception. Never guess prices or availability.

• Balneological screening:
Before booking a sulphur or peat bath the agent asks about cardiovascular contraindications.

• Immediate escalation:
Emergency symptoms (chest pain, shortness of breath) trigger a transfer to the on-duty nurse station.
s6_notes: In a health resort a wrong price is a commercial issue, but a hallucinated treatment is a health risk.
s7_title: Anna Doesn't Just Chat — She Acts in the PMS
s7_rows: Checks free treatment slots in the calendar
Books the guest and returns an ID (e.g. SPA-4821)
Cancels a treatment (free >2 h, 50% <2 h, 0% with medical release)
Moves a treatment to a new slot (free, new SPA code)
Checks room availability and calculates the total stay price
Sends an SMS / Telegram summary with the booking ID and directions
Hands off to reception / nurse station (log + Telegram alert)
s7_notes: Point out that the human handoff is simulated by a webhook in the PoC (log + Telegram alert) because there is no telephony/SIP — a native SIP REFER will replace it in production.
s8_ch1_title: Channel 1: Traditional Telephony (SIP Trunk) — target state
s8_ch1_body:
• Same agent and prompt once SIP Trunk is connected (Phase II — no telephony in the PoC)
• Direct number to the hotel reception
• 24/7 availability with no queueing
• Turn timeout 3.0 s, paraphrased confirmations, SMS after the call
s8_ch2_title: Channel 2: Interactive Web Widget on the Hotel Website
s8_ch2_body:
• Quick Reply Chips: pick a language (6 options) and a topic
• Live Transcript: follow the conversation in real time
• Success Card: instant booking confirmation with an option to send it to a carer
• Signed URL: 15-minute secure WebSocket token without exposing the API key
s8_notes: In the PoC the agent runs only as a web widget; the SIP Trunk phone channel is the target state with the very same agent configuration.
s9_scenarios: Path A: SPA Treatment Booking (Happy Path)
Guest asks about a therapeutic massage -> Anna checks the calendar -> proposes 14:30 -> paraphrases the details -> confirms booking SPA-4821 -> sends the SMS.
Question about diabetic meal times and the shuttle -> a precise answer from the knowledge base with no hallucination.
Guest reports cardiac symptoms before a sulphur bath -> Anna transfers to the nurse station immediately.
s9_notes: Have a fallback ready: if the network drops, show the FastAPI logs or the audio recordings.
s10_title: Enterprise Ready: GDPR & Medical Data Protection
s10_items: Audio and transcripts are processed in RAM only — nothing is written to ElevenLabs disks.
Automatic masking of personal (PII) and medical data in logs.
Data processed inside the European Union, full GDPR / DPA compliance.
Secure one-time tokens that keep the API key out of the browser.
s10_notes: For a hotel-chain board, medical compliance is a sine qua non condition.
s11_title: One Agent, Ten Hotels — Network Scaling
s11_panel_body:
• 1 Central Agent: instead of 10 separate bots we maintain a single system-prompt core.

• Dynamic Variables: injected when the call starts:
  - hotel_name, location
  - reception_phone
  - pms_hotel_id

• SIP UUI signalling: the PBX passes the hotel ID in the call headers.

• Scalability: adding an 11th property is 5 minutes of variable configuration.
s11_notes: Show how you think as a Deployment Strategist: maintenance cost and agent governance optimisation.
s12_title: Deployment Cost & Hard Return on Investment (ROI)
s12_roi_body:
• 275 min of AI ($22 ≈ 88 PLN) costs as much as 3.5 hours of a receptionist (~25 PLN/h).
• Revenue protection: three night room bookings (3 × 500 PLN = 1,500 PLN ≈ $375) cover the monthly Scale plan ($299).
• Value for staff: no burnout and full focus on guests physically present at the property.
s12_notes: Do not position AI as headcount reduction. It protects revenue at night and during call peaks. FX rate used: 4.0 PLN/USD; platform pricing as of 2026-11.
s13_title: Implementation Roadmap: from PoC to Proactive AI
s13_phases:
• RAG knowledge base (5 files)
• Mock backend (FastAPI, 7 webhook tools, :8011)
• Web widget with Quick Reply Chips
• Latency and prompt testing

• Direct PMS API (Opera/KWHotel)
• Twilio SMS gateway (confirmations)
• SIP PBX telephony integration
• Multilingual (DE, EN, UA)

• Automated pre-arrival calls
• Shuttle confirmation
• Personalised treatment recommendations
• Advanced intent and CSAT analytics
s13_notes: Phase III moves the agent from a reactive hotline to a proactive revenue generator.
